p:cNvPr.descr: The nucleic acids are represented by colored squares containing the first letter of the nucleic acid. Beginning at the top left with DNA (labeled above), the chain begins at the 5' end (labeled above). The chain begins with a phosphate group. O- bonds down to P, which bonds left to O-, double bonds right to O, and down to O. O bonds down to CH2, which is labeled at right with a small 5'. The CH2 marks the beginning of the pentose ring which repeats down the chain. CH2 bonds down to C, which bonds down to H and down & left to C. C bonds up to H and down to O, which is part of the next phosphodiester bond. Next to this there is a small 3'. C bonds right to C, which bonds up and down to H and up and right to C. C bonds up to a blue boxed A, down to H, and up and right to O, which bonds down and left to the C that began the chain. This constitutes a single pentose ring. The O bonds down to the next phosphate group, which is boxed in gray with text to the left reading, "phosphodiester linkage." The phosphate group's bottom O bonds down to another pentose ring, this one bonded to a yellow boxed T on the right. The bottom O bonds down to another phosphate group, which then bonds down to a final pentose ring bonded on the right to a green boxed G. Below that is the 3' end (labeled) indicating the end of the chain. To the right is an RNA chain, labeled at the top. It also begins at the 5' end. The chain begins single pentose ring. The O bonds down to the next phosphate group, which is boxed in gray with text to the left reading, "phosphodiester linkage." The phosphate group is bonded down to the first pentose ring, which is bonded right to a brown boxed U. This is bonded below to another phosphate group. The bottom O bonds down to another pentose ring, this one bonded to a green boxed G on the right. The bottom O bonds down to another phosphate group, which then bonds down to a final pentose ring bonded on the right to a pink boxed C. Below that is the 3' end (labeled) indicating the end of the chain.
